name: Burgruine Schrofenstein
kurzbeschreibung: The dramatic ruin of Burg Schrofenstein perches on a sheer rock needle above the distillery village of Stanz overlooking the Inn Valley.
preis: Free of charge (ruin forecourt and observation point)
oeffnungszeiten: Accessible year-round (snow-free months recommended; interior masonry closed for safety)
beschreibung:
Overview

The dramatically poised Burgruine Schrofenstein clings to a steep rock needle at an altitude of 1,122 meters high above the village of Stanz bei Landeck on the sunny southern slopes of the Lechtal Alps. As the ancient ancestral seat of the influential knightly dynasty of Schrofenstein, the cliff-top castle looks back on a turbulent history reaching into the 12th century. From their eagles' nest, the noble lords commanded the strategic traffic arteries of the upper Inn Valley, the gateway to the Arlberg Pass, and the entrance into the Paznaun. The imposing, nearly intact Romanesque keep constructed of solid rubble masonry is visible from miles around. Its daring location and romantic aura make Schrofenstein one of the most intriguing and photogenic historical landmarks in the entire Tyrolean Oberland.

Route & Requirements

The hike to the castle ruin starts in the sun-drenched schnapps-distilling village of Stanz bei Landeck. A well-marked hiking trail initially meanders past flowering fruit orchards and ancient chestnut groves, then winds in moderate switchbacks through shaded mountain forest up to the castle rock (approx. 45 minutes walking time, 220 vertical meters). The path is natural, rocky, and rooted, requiring ankle-high hiking shoes with grippy profile soles as well as reliable surefootedness. The fortress itself is an unmanaged ruin; entering the interior keep and crumbling walls is prohibited for safety reasons, but the forecourt provides an extraordinary vantage point. For surefooted families, the trail makes a rewarding short outing amid stunning alpine scenery.

Visit & Arrival

The forecourt and panoramic viewpoint of Burgruine Schrofenstein are freely accessible year-round; the optimal hiking season runs from April to November. In deep winter, shaded forest sections can be icy. By car, take the Inntal motorway A12 or expressway S16 (exit Landeck/Zams), turn off to Stanz, and park at the designated hikers' car park at the village edge. Rail travelers arrive at Landeck-Zams ÖBB station and take the local bus to Stanz or walk along the sunny Stanzer Steig in about 45 minutes.

Tips

Pair your ruin hike with a tasting visit to one of the renowned artisan schnapps distilleries in Stanz, celebrated for its Stanzer Zwetschke plum brandy. Bring a packed lunch and savour the breathtaking view from the castle terrace over Landeck and the Upper Inn Valley.
